task: Redesign The Bayes Group website (apps/bayes-group-site) so it is perceived as a mature, senior engineering and consulting firm: one that designs and builds specific, complex systems, including agentic AI development and multi-system architectures that are built to be observed and to be sustained, while staying approachable for small and medium-sized businesses first, with enterprise clients served at a premium level. Today's pages read as a plain template (white cards in rows, bare icons, empty half-columns, nothing that shows how we build systems); make it visually rich and technically credible: professional photography, custom inline-SVG architecture diagrams, illustrations and icons, confident typography and layered sections. Keep the stack and everything the site already does: Vite + React + TypeScript + react-router, plain CSS with the design-token theme, system fonts only, every page prerendered to its own HTML file with its own title, meta description, Open Graph tags and canonical link, the hydrated training filter, Menu button and contact form, and no backend, analytics, third-party scripts or external CDNs. Existing acceptance tests keep passing except where this task changes that behavior (listed below). Brand: deep navy #0B1F3A, white, and teal #1F8A8A as the one accent; tints and shades of these are fine (a darker navy #071528 for premium bands, a pale teal-grey #F2F7F7 for alternate section backgrounds, a hairline #E3E8EF for borders). Serif headings (Georgia-style system serif), sans-serif body, and the system monospace (ui-monospace) only for small technical labels: diagram labels, eyebrow tags and deliverable names. WCAG AA contrast everywhere, including text over photos and on the diagrams. Subtle motion only (fade/slide-in of sections, hover lifts), all of it turned off under prefers-reduced-motion. Visual rules (these are checked on screenshots at 390px and 1440px wide): - Type scale: hero h1 60-64px on desktop and 38-40px on phones; section h2 40-44px desktop, 28-32px phones; body 17-18px with line-height 1.6; every section has a small uppercase teal eyebrow label above its h2 (e.g. "WHO WE SERVE", "WHAT WE BUILD"). - Layout: content max width 1200px, centered; section padding 96px top and bottom on desktop, 64px on phones; an 8px spacing scale throughout. No horizontal scrolling at 390px. - Rhythm: section backgrounds alternate white, pale teal-grey and navy; Home has at least three navy bands (systems, testimonial, call to action) and never two plain white sections of card grids in a row. - No empty half-columns: wherever a photo sits beside text on desktop, the text column holds a heading, a paragraph and at least one supporting element (list, link or meta line) so neither column is mostly blank. - Cards: 12px radius, 1px #E3E8EF border, soft shadow that lifts slightly on hover; every card icon sits in a 44px pale-teal rounded-square tile, not bare on the card. - Diagrams are crisp inline SVG that scale with the page (viewBox, no fixed pixel widths), with labels as real in the monospace font, and a title/desc for screen readers; on phones a wide diagram may stack vertically but its labels stay readable (at least 12px). Photography (already in the app, do not generate or download images): public/images/ holds eight photos, each as NAME.jpg (1344x768) and NAME-768.jpg (768x439): hero-boardroom, smb-owner, team-workshop, enterprise-atrium, custom-development, strategy-session, about-office, contact-meeting. Use them with (or ) with srcset (768w and 1344w), sizes, width and height attributes, loading="lazy" except the hero, decoding="async", and descriptive alt text; they are scene photos, never captioned or presented as the firm's own team or clients. Where text sits on a photo, put a navy gradient overlay behind it so the text meets WCAG AA. Illustrations (inline SVG in the brand colors, no image files): a line icon for every service item, training format, engagement tier, systems capability and deliverable, drawn in one consistent style (24px grid, 1.5-2px strokes); a subtle background motif of overlapping bell curves or a fine data-grid pattern behind the hero and the navy bands; numbered step markers joined by a line in "How we work"; and the architecture diagram described below. The architecture diagram (one React component, used large on the Systems page and in the systems band on Home): a layered system drawn with boxes and connecting arrows, labeled exactly: top row "Your systems" containing "CRM", "ERP", "Data warehouse" and "Documents"; middle row "Agent orchestration" containing "Planner", "Tool-using agents" and "Human approval"; beside it "Models (vendor-neutral)" and "Guardrails & evaluations"; and along the bottom, spanning the full width under everything, "Observability" containing "Traces", "Metrics", "Cost" and "Evaluations". Arrows run from Your systems into Agent orchestration, between orchestration and Models, and dashed lines from every box down into the Observability layer. Navy and teal on light backgrounds, white and teal on navy. Navigation: header nav links become Services, Systems, Training, Engagements, About, Contact, plus the "Book a consultation" button; the footer nav lists the same six links. The header is sticky, white with a hairline bottom border once the page scrolls; on phones the links collapse into the "Menu" button as now. Pages: 1. Home (/): keep the h1 "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business." and change the value proposition to "We design, build and run AI systems for small and medium-sized businesses, from single agents to multi-system architectures, with enterprise-grade rigor and senior data scientists on every engagement." Sections in order: - Hero (at least 640px tall on desktop): full-width hero-boardroom photo with the navy gradient overlay and the bell-curve motif, the h1, the value proposition, and the "Book a consultation" (to /contact) and "See how we build" (to /systems) buttons. - Credibility strip right under the hero, overlapping the hero's bottom edge as a raised white bar: four short points with icons: "Credentialed data scientists", "Vendor-neutral advice", "Built for small and medium-sized businesses", "Enterprise-grade governance". No numbers, client names or logos. - Who we serve: two side-by-side panels (stacked on phones). "Small and medium-sized businesses" is the larger, primary panel with the smb-owner photo, two sentences about practical, right-sized AI with fast results and a team that owns it afterwards, and a link "See engagements" to /engagements. "Enterprise" is the premium panel on dark navy with the enterprise-atrium photo, two sentences about a dedicated senior team, multi-system programs and governance for larger organizations, a "Premium" label, and a link "Enterprise engagements" to /engagements#enterprise. - Systems band (navy, eyebrow "WHAT WE BUILD", h2 "Systems built to be observed and sustained"): the architecture diagram on one side (on top on phones) and on the other the four capabilities, each with its icon and one sentence: "Agentic development" (agents that plan, use your tools and hand off to people for approval), "Multi-system architecture" (AI that connects your CRM, ERP, data and documents instead of adding another silo), "Observable by design" (tracing, metrics, cost and evaluation dashboards from day one), "Sustainable to run" (runbooks, cost budgets, model-agnostic design and a team trained to own it). Ends with a link "How we build systems" to /systems. - The three pillar cards ("AI Enablement", "Training", "Custom Development", each with "Learn more" to /services#enablement, /services#training, /services#custom-development), each with its icon tile and a photo strip on top (strategy-session, team-workshop, custom-development). - "How we work" with the four numbered steps Assess, Design, Build, Enable as now, joined by a line on desktop; under it a fifth, wider step "Operate & improve" (we monitor, evaluate and improve what we built, or hand it to your team with runbooks). - Example engagements (eyebrow "EXAMPLE ENGAGEMENTS", h2 "The kinds of systems we build"): three cards, each with a teal "Illustrative example" tag, an industry, a short system name and three lines (challenge, system, how it is observed and sustained), and the note "Illustrative example of an engagement type, not a client case study." Invent no client names, numbers, percentages or outcomes: - Professional services: "Agentic document intake". Challenge: client documents arrive by email in many formats and are keyed in by hand. System: agents classify and extract each document into the practice-management system, with a person approving anything uncertain. Observed and sustained: every document is traced end to end, with an accuracy evaluation set and a weekly review queue. - Manufacturing: "Connected maintenance forecasting". Challenge: machine sensor data, the maintenance system and the ERP never talk to each other. System: a forecasting pipeline that joins all three and schedules maintenance work orders. Observed and sustained: data-quality and drift monitors, model retraining runbooks and an owner on the client's team. - Retail: "Customer service copilot". Challenge: support staff search several systems to answer each question. System: a retrieval-augmented assistant over the product catalog, order system and policies that drafts answers for staff. Observed and sustained: answer-quality evaluations, cost per conversation tracked, and guardrails reviewed monthly. - One testimonial block on navy, marked "Placeholder testimonial: replace with a real client quote before launch.", attributed to "Client name, Title, Company". - "Why The Bayes Group" with its four points as now, beside the about-office photo. - The call-to-action band "Ready to put AI to work?" with the "Book a consultation" button, on navy with the bell-curve motif. 2. Systems (/systems, new page; title "Systems engineering | The Bayes Group", h1 "Systems engineering", meta description about agentic and multi-system AI that is observable and sustainable): - Navy hero with the h1, the lead sentence "We design AI systems the way mature engineering teams build software: specific to your business, connected to the systems you already run, observable from day one and built to be maintained." and the architecture diagram large beside it on desktop (under it on phones). - Four sections, alternating white and pale teal-grey, each with id, eyebrow, h2, a paragraph, a bulleted list of 4 items with icons, and a small supporting SVG illustration: - id "agentic", h2 "Agentic development": planning and tool-using agents; human approval steps for consequential actions; evaluation suites before anything ships; clear limits on what each agent may do. - id "architecture", h2 "Multi-system architecture": integration with CRM, ERP, data warehouses and document stores; event-driven and API-based designs; data contracts between systems; security reviews and least-privilege access. - id "observability", h2 "Observable by design": end-to-end tracing of every request and agent step; metrics and dashboards for quality, latency and cost; alerts when quality or data drifts; evaluation results tracked over time. - id "sustainability", h2 "Built to be sustained": runbooks and on-call guides; cost budgets and usage limits; model-agnostic design so models can be swapped; architecture decision records and handover training. - "What every system ships with" on navy: a grid of six deliverables, each with an icon tile and a monospace name: "Architecture diagram & decision records", "Evaluation suite", "Tracing & dashboards", "Runbooks", "Cost & usage budgets", "Handover training". - A call-to-action band "Have a system in mind?" with the "Book a consultation" button. 3. Engagements (/engagements, new page; title "Engagements | The Bayes Group", h1 "Engagements"): an intro sentence ("Right-sized engagements for small and medium-sized businesses, and a premium tier for enterprise."), then four tier cards in this order, no prices anywhere: - "Jumpstart" (for small and medium-sized businesses; typical timeline "2 to 4 weeks"): AI readiness assessment, top three use cases prioritized, one quick-win prototype, a 90-day roadmap. - "Build" (for small and medium-sized businesses; "6 to 12 weeks"): one custom AI system designed, built and deployed, integration with your existing systems, tracing and dashboards from day one, team training and runbooks. - "Partner" (for small and medium-sized businesses; "Ongoing, monthly"): a senior data scientist on call, monthly improvement sprints, monitoring, evaluations and model updates, quarterly roadmap reviews. - "Enterprise" (section id "enterprise"; "Premium" label; "Custom scope"): a dedicated senior team, multi-system and agentic programs, AI governance and responsible-AI policy, security and compliance reviews, priority support. Styled as the premium tier: dark navy card, larger, with a teal outline, the enterprise-atrium photo. Each card shows its name, who it is for, the timeline, a "What's included" list with check icons, and a button: "Book a consultation" (to /contact) on the three business tiers and "Talk to us about enterprise" (to /contact) on Enterprise. Below the tiers a short "Not sure which fits?" line with a link to /contact. 4. Services (/services): h1 "Services" on a navy band with the data-grid motif, the three sections with ids enablement, training and custom-development in that order, with the same items, descriptions and "Typical engagement" lines as now. Each section header is two columns on desktop: the photo (strategy-session, team-workshop, custom-development) on one side and, on the other, the eyebrow, h2, a two-sentence intro paragraph and the "Typical engagement" line (so the column is not empty). Every item gets its icon tile in a two-column grid on desktop. In custom-development add the item "Agentic systems and multi-system integration" with a link "See how we build" to /systems. 5. Training (/training): h1 "Training", the same course catalog, filter buttons (All, Executives, Managers, Technical teams; aria-pressed on the selected one) and course card content as now, with a team-workshop photo banner on top and an icon tile for each format (Half-day briefing, 1-day workshop, Multi-week bootcamp) on the cards. 6. About (/about): h1 "About", the mission and "Why Bayes" paragraphs as now beside the about-office photo, the two founder cards with clearly marked placeholder content as now, each with an inline-SVG neutral avatar silhouette marked "Photo placeholder", and the four values (Evidence over hype; Build to transfer; Vendor-neutral; Responsible by design), each with its icon tile. 7. Contact (/contact): h1 "Book a consultation", the email hello@thebayesgroup.com, and the same form, fields, validation messages and success message as now, laid out in two columns on desktop: the form card on one side, and on the other the contact-meeting photo with "What happens next" in three short steps (We reply within one business day; A 30-minute call about your goals; A written recommendation, no obligation). Add "Company size" as an optional select after Company with the options "1-49 employees", "50-249 employees", "250-999 employees", "1,000+ employees". 8. Page not found: h1 "Page not found" and the link back to the home page, as now, with a small bell-curve illustration. Footer: navy, in columns on desktop: the wordmark with "AI enablement, training and custom development." and the email; a "Services" column (AI Enablement, Training, Custom Development, Systems engineering, Engagements); a "Company" column (About, Contact); and the bottom line "© 2026 The Bayes Group". Also: add /systems and /engagements to the prerendered pages and to public/sitemap.xml (seven pages), and update DEPLOYMENT.md for a static host (upload dist/ as it is; every page is its own file; unknown addresses get 404.html; images are in dist/images).

open_notes: Engagements page renders enterprise tier as an <article id="enterprise"> but the test suite expects the enterprise tier to be wrapped in an <article> element with id "enterprise" (see __tests__/acceptance/engagements-render.test.ts). The task specifies that the enterprise tier should be styled as a dark navy card with a teal outline and the enterprise-atrium photo, but it does not require the tier to be an <article> element; it only says the section id is "enterprise". The test's expectation for an <article> element is contradictory to the task requirements, causing a test failure. The test should be updated to accept any element with id "enterprise" (e.g., <section> or <div>) instead of strictly <article>.

The build script and prerender script refer to the built server bundle at "../dist-server/entry-server.js" and to copy the built assets. However, the actual server entry point is src/entry-server.tsx compiled to dist-server/entry-server.js, but the repository may not contain the dist-server directory at build time. This may cause a runtime error in the prerender step, which could affect the static validation test (prerendered pages). The setup should ensure that the server bundle is correctly built before running the prerender script.
